'''Joseph Incandela''' is an American [[particle physics|particle physicist]], a professor of physics at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] and currently based at [[CERN]], where he spent two years as the spokesperson for the [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] experiment at the [[Large Hadron Collider]].

==Biography==
Incandela received his PhD from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1986. He worked on the UA2 experiment at CERN to study the recently discovered W and Z bosons before searching for charged Higgs bosons. He then moved back to the US in 1991 to work at FNAL, where he led the construction and design of silicon detectors and co-led the search for the top quark using lifetime tagging of b quark jets. This channel had the strongest contribution to the top quark discovery in 1995. Since 1997 he has been involved with the [[Large Hadron Collider]] at [[CERN]], initially leading the construction of a large part of the tracking system for the [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] (CMS) experiment. In 2011 he was elected to be the spokesperson for the CMS experiment.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ia.ucsb.edu/pa/display.aspx?pkey=2455 |title=UCSB Press Release: "UCSB Physicist Elected to Head CMS Experiment at Large Hadron Collider " |publisher=Ia.ucsb.edu |access-date=2012-09-21}}</ref>

On July 4, 2012, Incandela announced the discovery of the [[Higgs Boson]].<ref>{{cite news|author=Ian Sample at Cern, Geneva |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2012/jul/04/higgs-boson-cern-scientists-discover |title=Higgs boson: it's unofficial! Cern scientists discover missing particle &#124; Science &#124; guardian.co.uk |publisher=Guardian |date= 2012-07-04|access-date=2012-09-21 |location=London}}</ref>

Incandela was succeeded as CMS spokesperson by Tiziano Camporesi in January 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cms.web.cern.ch/news/tiziano-camporesi-takes-reins-cms |title=Tiziano Camporesi takes reins of CMS |publisher=cms.web.cern.ch |date=2014-01-10 |access-date=2014-03-12}}</ref> Profile article on Incandela back at UCSB.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news.ucsb.edu/2014/014276/coming-home-again |title=Coming Home Again |publisher=news.ucsb.edu |date=2014-06-18 |access-date=2015-12-24}}</ref>

==Awards and recognitions==
*On December 11, 2012, he was awarded the 2012 Special [[Fundamental Physics Prize]].<ref name=FPP-Dec2012>{{cite web|title=Fundamental Physics Prize - News |url=http://www.fundamentalphysicsprize.org/news3 |publisher=Fundamental Physics Prize |access-date=11 December 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014003742/http://fundamentalphysicsprize.org/news3 |archive-date=14 October 2013 }}</ref><ref name=FPS-Dec2012>{{cite web|title=Fundamental Physics Prize - Scholarship/Education programs|url=http://www.fundamentalphysicsprize.org/news5|publisher=Fundamental Physics Prize|access-date=11 October 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014044748/http://fundamentalphysicsprize.org/news5|archive-date=2013-10-14}}</ref>
* Elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news.ucsb.edu/2015/015364/incandela-elected-national-academy-sciences |title=Incandela Elected to the National Academy of Sciences |publisher=news.ucsb.edu |date=2015-04-28 |access-date=2015-12-24}}</ref>
